$SPY Checkout this video of me Predicting SPY’s Drop Before the Open today Using GEX 📉 

Back to basics for Monday, May 18 — about 10 minutes before the open, SPY was still showing a short gamma environment carried over from Friday’s premarket positioning. Market makers remained in negative gamma, which usually creates a more volatile trading environment with faster price movement and less stability.

The overall positioning also leaned bearish as the put-to-call ratio became even more negative than Friday’s reading. Looking at the gamma exposure by strike, the strongest levels were sitting below SPY’s current price near 739. The 735 and 730 strikes both showed roughly 5% normalized negative gamma exposure, making them the key levels on the board to watch to the downside.

On the other hand, there was still positive gamma sitting overhead near 745. But with SPY already trading in negative gamma at 739, a move lower looked more realistic than an upside push toward 745. In negative gamma environments, dealer hedging can accelerate momentum instead of slowing it down, which often increases volatility during selloffs.

The setup going into the open was fairly straightforward: daily net gamma remained negative, downside gamma exposure was building below price,  not convincing enough to justify aggressively buying calls. In this type of environment, patience and positioning tend to matter more than forcing bullish trades.

tweets.text:
SPX GEX LEVELS: May 18

The cliff hit harder than forecasted. Here's what the market looks like on the other side.

🚨🚨Monday's expected range: 7,300 – 7,475. The widest range since the March selloff. Direction depends on whether the flip at 7,405 holds.

Friday's monthly OPEX drained 36.8% of SPY's gamma cushion, not the 24.3% we projected. 2.61M gamma shares and 16.85M delta shares expired in a single session. The largest gamma rolloff since we started tracking. The engine that powered eight weeks of compressed ranges and mechanical dip-buying lost more than a third of its fuel in one close.

The numbers tell the story. Net GEX dropped 54%, from the all-time high of $1.64B on Thursday to $753M after OPEX. The 7,500 strike that carried +$310M on Thursday now reads +$105M. The 7,400 magnet that held +$191M is now +$62M. Every magnet weakened. Every level is thinner.

And the GEX flip is at spot again. The highest flip level sits at 7,405. SPX closed at 7,408.50. Three points of cushion. The third time in the series spot has landed on the regime threshold, FOMC week at 1 point, May 5 at 13 points, and now 3 points. But this time the gamma underneath is 54% lighter than the FOMC knife edge and 34% lighter than the May 5 scare. If the flip breaks, there's less structure to catch it.

The zone below the flip is the widest accelerator field in the series. Everything from 7,000 to 7,275 is negative gamma. The 7,300 strike is barely positive at +$5M. If spot slips below 7,405, the next meaningful support is at 7,400 (+$62M), then 7,375 (+$19M), then a long stretch of nothing before 7,300. The cushion that caught every dip for two months is structurally thinner now.

Above spot, the magnets still pull. 7,450 (+$82M), 7,500 (+$105M), 7,600 (+$81M). The center of gravity sits at 7,537, 1.7% above spot. The bullish skew is intact. If the flip holds, the magnets still function and the grind continues with wider daily ranges.

Here's the structural shift: the gamma blanket went from absorbing every headline with barely a flinch to a thinner structure where dips go deeper, rallies overshoot, and the range expands. The compression that made this rally feel effortless is mechanically weakened. Not gone; $753M is still positive gamma. But the market moves more freely now in both directions.

The rising wedge enters day 12. SPX pulled back 93 points from the 7,501 ATH. SPY closed at $739.12, still above the $732.28 breakdown level. The wedge hasn't triggered on consecutive-close criteria. But the OPEX drain is the structural catalyst the pattern was waiting for: thinner gamma means less resistance to the breakdown if it comes.

Wednesday is NVDA. Consensus at ~$1.75 EPS and ~$68B revenue. The market is pricing a +/- 6.4% move. Our Alphatica Earnings Model prediction drops before the report. NVDA is the tiebreaker, a beat into the thin blanket lifts the magnets and the buy signals win. A miss into 54% less gamma has no cushion underneath. The rising wedge resolves one way or the other by Thursday's close.

tweets.text:
Rolling daily $SPX GEX snapshots have been somewhat irrelevant since spring 2022.

That's when Tue/Thu SPX expiries were added and 0DTE became an everyday phenomenon. 

A single daily reading aggregates over three properties of today's market that the headline number can't capture:

—————
1) It's intraday-dynamic.

- Three key variables move at once through the session: 
Spot crosses strikes, 
- 0DTE positions are opened, closed and rolled (so dealer inventory itself shifts, not just where spot sits within it), 
- Time decays toward the cash close.

The gamma profile at 10:00 isn't the one at 14:30.

—————
2) It's extremely localized at the strike, and grows quasi-exponentially as expiration approaches.

Same ATM strike, 1h vs 3d to expiry: peak gamma multiple folds higher and the profile far narrower (chart below).

Stack that across every active 0DTE strike near spot and you get the spiky, migratory surface dealers actually hedge.

—————
3) It's not comparable to pre-2022.

Position distribution, the share of risk sitting in 0DTEs, and the speed at which positioning rotates intraday are all structurally different from the weekly/monthly regime that came before.

A 2024 print and a 2019 print aren't measuring the same object.

—————
PS:

What's actually shown is more a proxy for net OI in proximity to spot — naive GEX, with calls assumed bought by MMs and puts sold by them. 

That sign convention was always a shortcut, and in a regime where positioning flips intraday, anchoring to a daily snapshot of it is shakier still.

⚠️THIS IS UNPRECEDENTED:

The S&P 500 Gamma has surged from deeply negative levels at the end of March to the highest since 2021, the fastest surge EVER.

The only comparable episode was late 2021, when a similarly extreme gamma setup preceded a market top by just 1-2 months.

Gamma measures how much market makers must buy or sell in stock futures to hedge their options positions. 

When gamma is positive and rising, market makers act as a stabilizing force, buying dips and selling rallies. 

When it swings this violently from negative to positive, it signals an extraordinarily unstable market structure underneath a calm surface.

This has been driven by extreme speculation, particularly in the semiconductor stocks.

When a market reversal comes, it will be sharp and severe.
